product.name: Dropbox API (DBX Platform), not Dropbox Sign

source.quote: When you first create a Dropbox API app, it's given development status and can only be connected to your own account.

oauthAppCreation.where: Dropbox App Console: create an app, then choose scopes on its Permissions tab

source.quote: When you start building an app on the DBX Platform, you'll need to create a Dropbox app in the App Console

reviewGate.trigger: A new app is in development status (own account plus a limited number of others, up to 500). Opening it to more users needs production approval, reviewed once the app has linked at least 50 users.

source.quote: However, if you'd like to open your app to more users, you'll need to apply for production status.

approvalWait.stated: Dropbox responds to nearly all production requests within a few business days
approvalWait.derivation: A few business days is read as at most about a week; the figure is not numeric in the source

source.quote: We respond to nearly all production requests within a few business days.

testBeforeApproval.how: Development status works like production for up to 500 linked users; enable extra users from the app's info page

source.quote: it can only be linked with up to 500 total Dropbox users

blockers.summary: Once 50 users are linked, the app has two weeks to get production approval or it is frozen for new users

source.quote: your app's ability to link additional Dropbox users will be frozen until you submit an application and are approved for production status

blockers.summary: A production request is not reviewed until the app has linked at least 50 Dropbox users

source.quote: it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users

blockers.summary: Development status caps the app at 500 linked users

source.quote: it can only be linked with up to 500 total Dropbox users

blockers.summary: Reviewers check that the app does not request broader permissions than its functionality needs

source.quote: we'll review that your app doesn't request an unnecessarily broad permission based on the functionality provided by the app

avoidProducts.name: Dropbox Sign (HelloSign) API
avoidProducts.why: A separate e-signature product with its own API and keys
avoidProducts.evidence: Dropbox Sign admin pages appeared in web search results for the Dropbox API (2026-10-29)

notes: Scope strings come from Dropbox's official API spec repository (github.com/dropbox/dropbox-api-spec) because the scope reference on dropbox.com is rendered by script. It is Dropbox's own repo, but not a docs domain. Please confirm you accept it as an official source.
The wait is not numeric in the source (a few business days), so confidence is low.
